requirements.original: This annex specifies the matching mechanisms that may be used in TTCN-3 templates (and only in templates).
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism specified in annex B MAY be used in a template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.0 -- This annex specifies the matching mechanisms that may be used in TTCN-3 templates (and only in templates).

requirements.original: This annex specifies the matching mechanisms that may be used in TTCN-3 templates (and only in templates).
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism SHALL NOT be used outside of a template.

ambiguity.issue: '(and only in templates)' does not say whether e.g. template instances in in-line templates, template variables and template formal parameters count as 'templates'; the broad reading (any template-typed context) is chosen.
readings: A matching mechanism SHALL NOT be used anywhere except in a template, template variable, template formal parameter or in-line template.
A matching mechanism SHALL NOT be used anywhere except in a global or local template definition.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.0 -- This annex specifies the matching mechanisms that may be used in TTCN-3 templates (and only in templates).

requirements.original: Unless otherwise specified, a template field matches the corresponding field value if, and only if, the field value has exactly the same value as the value to which the expression in the template evaluates.
requirements.canonical: Unless otherwise specified, a template field containing a specific value matches the corresponding field value if, and only if, the field value is exactly the same value as the value to which the expression in the template field evaluates.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.1 -- Unless otherwise specified, a template field matches the corresponding field value if, and only if, the field value has exactly the same value as the value to which the expression in the template evaluates.

requirements.original: The following matching mechanisms may be used in place of explicit values.
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism of clauses B.1.2.1 to B.1.2.x MAY be used in a template in place of an explicit value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.0 -- The following matching mechanisms may be used in place of explicit values.

requirements.original: It can be used for values of all types.
requirements.canonical: A template list MAY be used for values of all types.

examples.text:
template MyMessageType mw_myTemplate:= 
  { 
     field1 := (2,4,6),   // list of integer values 
     field2 := ("String1", "String2"), // list of charstring values 
     :
     :
  }

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- It can be used for values of all types.

requirements.original: A template list may contain values, templates obeying the template (present) restriction (see clause 15.8), and members added by all from clauses.
requirements.canonical: A template list MAY contain values, templates obeying the present template restriction and members added by `all from` clauses.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- A template list may contain values, templates obeying the template (present) restriction (see clause 15.8), and members added by all from clauses.

requirements.original: An all from clause comprises all elements of an existing record of or set of template into the template list.
requirements.canonical: An `all from` clause in a template list inserts all elements of the referenced existing record of or set of template into the template list.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- An all from clause comprises all elements of an existing record of or set of template into the template list.

requirements.original: An all from clause comprises all elements of an existing record of or set of template into the template list.
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a template list SHALL be a record of or set of template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- An all from clause comprises all elements of an existing record of or set of template into the template list.

requirements.original: A template field that uses a template list matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value matches any one of the values or templates in the template list, after resolving all all from clauses.
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses a template list matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value matches any one of the values or templates in the template list after all `all from` clauses have been resolved.

examples.text:
template MyMessageType mw_myTemplate:= 
  { 
     field1 := (2,4,6),   // list of integer values 
     field2 := ("String1", "String2"), // list of charstring values 
     :
     :
  }

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- A template field that uses a template list matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value matches any one of the values or templates in the template list, after resolving all all from clauses.

requirements.original: Each value or template in the template list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which this mechanism is used. d) Each value or template in the template list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which this mechanism is used.
requirements.canonical: Each value or template in a template list SHALL be of the type declared for the template or template field in which the template list is used.

ambiguity.issue: 'template field' is used although a template list may also be used for a template as a whole (EXAMPLE 2: mw_i1); the rule applies to the type of the template or template field.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- Each value or template in the template list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which this mechanism is used. d) Each value or template in the template list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which this mechanism is used.

requirements.original: a) The type of the template list and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.
requirements.canonical: The type of a template list and the member type of the template referenced in an `all from` clause of that template list SHALL be compatible.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- a) The type of the template list and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.

requirements.original: b) The template in the all from clause shall be either a specific value or combined template.
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a template list SHALL be either a specific value or a combined template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- b) The template in the all from clause shall be either a specific value or combined template.

requirements.original: Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.
requirements.canonical: An element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a template list MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute except AnyElementsOrNone and permutation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

requirements.original: c) Individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to any of the following matching mechanisms: AnyElementsOrNone, permutation.
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a template list SHALL NOT resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- c) Individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to any of the following matching mechanisms: AnyElementsOrNone, permutation.

requirements.original: e) Templates in the template list shall obey the template (present) restriction (see clause 15.8).
requirements.canonical: A template contained in a template list SHALL obey the present template restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.1 -- e) Templates in the template list shall obey the template (present) restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.original: It can be used on all values of all types.
requirements.canonical: A complemented template list MAY be used for values of all types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- It can be used on all values of all types.

requirements.original: A complemented value list may also contain templates obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).
requirements.canonical: A complemented template list MAY contain templates obeying the present template restriction.

ambiguity.issue: 'complemented value list' is used for the complemented template list.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- A complemented value list may also contain templates obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.original: A template field that uses complement matches the corresponding field if and only if the corresponding field's value does not match any of the values or templates listed in the template list.
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses a complemented template list matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value does not match any of the values or templates listed in the complemented template list.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- A template field that uses complement matches the corresponding field if and only if the corresponding field's value does not match any of the values or templates listed in the template list.

requirements.original: The template list may be a single value, of course.
requirements.canonical: A complemented template list MAY consist of a single value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- The template list may be a single value, of course.

requirements.original: Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of an existing record of or set of template into a complement template list using an all from clause.
requirements.canonical: An `all from` clause MAY be used in a complemented template list to add all elements of an existing record of or set of template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of an existing record of or set of template into a complement template list using an all from clause.

requirements.original: a) The type of the complemented template list and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.
requirements.canonical: The type of a complemented template list and the member type of the template referenced in an `all from` clause of that list SHALL be compatible.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- a) The type of the complemented template list and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.

requirements.original: b) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a specific value or combined template.
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a complemented template list SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- b) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a specific value or combined template.

requirements.original: Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.
requirements.canonical: An element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a complemented template list MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute except AnyElementsOrNone and permutation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

requirements.original: c) Individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to any of the following matching mechanisms: AnyElementsOrNone, permutation.
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a complemented template list SHALL NOT resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- c) Individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to any of the following matching mechanisms: AnyElementsOrNone, permutation.

requirements.original: d) Each value or template in the list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which the complement is used.
requirements.canonical: Each value or template in a complemented template list SHALL be of the type declared for the template or template field in which the complement is used.

ambiguity.issue: 'template field' is used although `complement` may also be used for a template as a whole (EXAMPLE 2: mw_i1).

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- d) Each value or template in the list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which the complement is used.

requirements.original: e) The complement of a template list shall not match omit.
requirements.canonical: A complemented template list SHALL NOT match `omit`.

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated whether 'shall not match omit' means that a complemented template list never matches an absent optional field, or that `omit` is not allowed as a member of the list.
readings: A complemented template list SHALL NOT match an absent (omitted) optional field.
A complemented template list SHALL NOT contain `omit` as a member.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- e) The complement of a template list shall not match omit.

requirements.original: f) Templates in the complement of a template list shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).
requirements.canonical: A template contained in a complemented template list SHALL obey the present template restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.2 -- f) Templates in the complement of a template list shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.original: The matching symbol "?" (AnyValue) matches any value of the specified type.
requirements.canonical: The AnyValue matching symbol `?` matches any value of the specified type.

examples.text:
template MyMessageType mw_myTemplate:=
  { 
     field1 := ?, // will match any integer 
     field2 := ?, // will match any non-empty charstring value 
     field3 := ?, // will match true or false 
     field4 := ?    // will match any sequence of integers 
  }

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.3 -- The matching symbol "?" (AnyValue) matches any value of the specified type.

requirements.original: It can be used on values of all types.
requirements.canonical: AnyValue (`?`) MAY be used for values of all types.

examples.text:
template MyMessageType mw_myTemplate:=
  { 
     field1 := ?, // will match any integer 
     field2 := ?, // will match any non-empty charstring value 
     field3 := ?, // will match true or false 
     field4 := ?    // will match any sequence of integers 
  }

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.3 -- It can be used on values of all types.

requirements.original: A template field that uses the any value mechanism matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field evaluates to a single element of the specified type.
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses AnyValue (`?`) matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field evaluates to a single element of the specified type.

ambiguity.issue: 'evaluates to a single element of the specified type' is not defined; it is chosen to mean that the field is present with any value (so an absent optional field does not match).
readings: A template field that uses AnyValue matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field is present and holds any value of its type.
A template field that uses AnyValue matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field holds exactly one value (not a list) of its type.

examples.text:
template MyMessageType mw_myTemplate:=
  { 
     field1 := ?, // will match any integer 
     field2 := ?, // will match any non-empty charstring value 
     field3 := ?, // will match true or false 
     field4 := ?    // will match any sequence of integers 
  }

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.3 -- A template field that uses the any value mechanism matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field evaluates to a single element of the specified type.

requirements.original: The matching symbol "*" (AnyValueOrNone) is used to indicate that any valid value and the omission of the given optional field are acceptable.
requirements.canonical: The AnyValueOrNone matching symbol `*` indicates that any valid value and the omission of the given optional field are acceptable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.4 -- The matching symbol "*" (AnyValueOrNone) is used to indicate that any valid value and the omission of the given optional field are acceptable.

requirements.original: It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to a value associated with a key of a map template. a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) MAY be assigned to a template of any type as a whole, to an optional field of a set or record template, or to a value associated with a key of a map template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.4 -- It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to a value associated with a key of a map template. a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.original: A record or set template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, either the field evaluates to any element of the specified type, or if the field is absent.
requirements.canonical: A record or set template field that uses AnyValueOrNone (`*`) matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field evaluates to any element of the specified type or the field is absent.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.4 -- A record or set template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, either the field evaluates to any element of the specified type, or if the field is absent.

requirements.original: A map template key that uses this symbol instead of an associated value matches the corresponding key if, and only if, either the corresponding key is present and its associated value evaluates to any value of the specified type, or if the corresponding key is absent.
requirements.canonical: A map template key that uses AnyValueOrNone (`*`) instead of an associated value matches the corresponding key if, and only if, the key is present and its associated value evaluates to any value of the specified type, or the key is absent.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.4 -- A map template key that uses this symbol instead of an associated value matches the corresponding key if, and only if, either the corresponding key is present and its associated value evaluates to any value of the specified type, or if the corresponding key is absent.

requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) SHALL NOT be assigned to a mandatory field of a record or set template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.4 -- a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.original: b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.
requirements.canonical: At the time of matching during a receiving operation, AnyValueOrNone (`*`) SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether a template that is `*` as a whole (allowed by restriction a) may be used directly in a receiving operation, and whether a violation is a compile-time or a runtime error. The reading that a top-level `*` is not allowed in a receiving operation is chosen.
readings: A template that is AnyValueOrNone as a whole SHALL NOT be used as the top-level template of a receiving operation; `*` is only effective in optional fields and map values.
A template that is AnyValueOrNone as a whole MAY be used in a receiving operation only when it is referenced from an optional field or map value; otherwise the matching causes a runtime error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.4 -- b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.

requirements.original: A template field that uses a range matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value is equal to one of the values in the range.
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses a value range matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value is equal to one of the values in the range.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.5 -- A template field that uses a range matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value is equal to one of the values in the range.

requirements.original: a) When used for values of integer or float types (and integer or float subtypes), a boundary value shall be either: 1) infinity or -infinity; 2) an expression that evaluates to a specific integer or float value.
requirements.canonical: When a value range is used for values of integer or float types (or their subtypes), each boundary SHALL be either `infinity`, `-infinity`, or an expression that evaluates to a specific integer or float value.
requirements.condition: the range is used for values of integer or float types or subtypes
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.5 -- a) When used for values of integer or float types (and integer or float subtypes), a boundary value shall be either: 1) infinity or -infinity; 2) an expression that evaluates to a specific integer or float value.

requirements.original: b) The lower boundary shall be put on the left side of the range, the upper boundary at the right side.
requirements.canonical: The lower boundary of a value range SHALL be placed on the left side of the range and the upper boundary on the right side.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.5 -- b) The lower boundary shall be put on the left side of the range, the upper boundary at the right side.

requirements.original: The lower boundary shall be less than the upper boundary.
requirements.canonical: The lower boundary of a value range SHALL be less than the upper boundary.

ambiguity.issue: 'less than' can be read strictly (a range such as (1..1) is an error) or as 'not greater than'; it is also unclear how exclusive boundaries (!) are taken into account. The strict literal reading is chosen.
readings: The lower boundary of a value range SHALL be strictly less than the upper boundary.
The lower boundary of a value range SHALL be less than or equal to the upper boundary.
The value range SHALL contain at least one value after applying exclusive boundaries.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.5 -- The lower boundary shall be less than the upper boundary.

requirements.original: c) When used in templates or template fields of charstring or universal charstring types, the boundaries shall evaluate to valid character positions according to the coded character set table(s) of the type (e.g. the given position shall not be empty).
requirements.canonical: When a value range is used in a template or template field of charstring or universal charstring type, each boundary SHALL evaluate to a valid, non-empty character position according to the coded character set table(s) of the type.
requirements.condition: the range is used for charstring or universal charstring types
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.5 -- c) When used in templates or template fields of charstring or universal charstring types, the boundaries shall evaluate to valid character positions according to the coded character set table(s) of the type (e.g. the given position shall not be empty).

requirements.original: d) Empty positions between the lower and the upper boundaries are not considered to be valid values of the specified range.
requirements.canonical: An empty character position between the lower and the upper boundary of a value range IS NOT a valid value of that range.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.5 -- d) Empty positions between the lower and the upper boundaries are not considered to be valid values of the specified range.
